correctness.rationale: In the canonical 0/1 Euclidean embedding, the squared distance is the cardinality of the symmetric difference. The published adjacency criterion is a single alternating path/cycle. Four disjoint classes are exhaustively counted with factors for pair selection, orientation, ordering and reversal, yielding the displayed polynomial for every n>=2, 0<=k<=floor(n/2). With A_{k,j}=C(k,j)2^{j-1}j!, the exact identity A_{k,k-r}/A_{k,k}=1/(2^r r!) and a cycle-to-path ratio 1/j yield Poisson(1/2) plus an independent three-point type shift at fixed uncovered count. The cycle mass is bounded by O(1/k) plus a vanishing factorial tail. A separate connectivity-based enumeration reproduced every squared-length coefficient for 34 finite matching-size strata, n=2,...,10. Neither numerical approximations nor failed tests are used as proofs.

value.rationale: Determines a natural complete Euclidean local invariant of the classical K_n matching polytope and its rank-wise metric spectrum for all dimensions, not merely a relabeling of degree. The sharp fixed-uncovered-count Poisson defect makes a substantive distinction between almost-all extremely long edges at a near-perfect matching and the published existence of a global Hamilton traversal using only length-at-most-three edits. This contrast motivates both the exact histogram and the limiting distribution. The result is self-contained conditional on the explicitly credited classical adjacency theorem.
